subject: Sev-2: Partial inference degradation — Brightleaf impact & remediation plan
messages:
From: ops-alerts@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] Inference node error spike (region: us-west2)

Monitoring detected a spike in error rates for the text-generation endpoint serving the Brightleaf deployment. Errors: increased 5xx responses and timeouts between 09:06–09:11 PDT.

Summary:
- Affected capacity: ~15% of dedicated pool for Brightleaf (us-west2).
- Symptom: high tail latency and intermittent 5xx on longer sequences (>512 tokens).
- Impact: user-facing timeouts for a subset of requests; customers report retries.

Action recommended: pager on-call + coordinate with customer ops.

Alert details / snapshot attached: support-snapshot-logs.txt

--
Redwood Monitoring

Hi Alice / Brightleaf ops team —

Thanks for the heads-up alert. I’m stepping in as the customer liaison for this event. We see the same error spike on our telemetry. Rishi (on-call infra) and Ben (account lead) are looped in.

What we’re doing now (first 30 min):
- Rishi: triaging root cause and isolating impacted hosts; will mitigate with a routing bypass to healthy nodes.
- I: notifying Brightleaf of scope and ETA.

Short-term expectations:
- We’ll apply a routing bypass and validate stability within 30–45 minutes.
- If bypass successful, we’ll keep to a rolling remediation and monitor for regressions.

I’ll send a customer-facing update in the next 30–45 minutes with confirmed mitigation steps and timeline.

Best,

Subject: Re: Sev-2: Partial inference degradation — Brightleaf impact & remediation plan

Stephanie / Brightleaf — quick tech update:

Root-candidate: a pathological sequence-length distribution combined with a kernel-level memory pressure on a small subset of nodes. Longer sequences are inflating KV-cache usage and pushing one optimized kernel path into a fallback that currently has a bug -> transient 5xx.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:00–10:03 PDT):
- Bypassed 4 nodes showing repeated 5xx and rebalanced traffic to healthy nodes.
- Disabled a recent kernel fallback flag for the affected model variant to force the stable execution path.
- Reduced the per-worker max-concurrency on the affected pool to limit amplification.

Observed result (10:04–10:10 PDT): error-rate dropped to baseline; tail latency improving. We will keep the bypass for 2 hours while we complete a deeper fix and validate.

Attachments: runbook-sev2.pdf (contain steps and rollback plan).

Planned next steps:
- 11:00 PDT: validate under controlled load; if green, start incremental reintroduction of nodes.
- 12:30 PDT: ship a targeted runtime patch to resolve the fallback path behavior; patch release includes safe-mode default.
- Post-incident: full postmortem and code PR with regression tests.

Ben — please confirm we should keep Brightleaf on the bypass for 2 hours and whether they need an IP block or additional rate-limits applied from our side.

Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Brightleaf — customer update: mitigation complete and next steps

Alice / Brightleaf execs / Ops —

Executive summary:
- Impact: A subset of Brightleaf inference requests experienced increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx between ~09:05–10:04 PDT affecting ~15% of your dedicated capacity.
- Current state: We applied traffic bypasses and conservative concurrency limits; telemetry shows error rates returned to baseline and tail latency improved. No data loss or model corruption observed.
- User impact: Some end-users may have seen retries/timeouts during the window. We estimate fewer than 0.5% of total requests experienced a client-visible failure.

What we did (high level):
- Isolated and removed 4 unhealthy nodes from traffic, disabled a risky kernel fallback, and stabilized the pool.
- Kept redundant capacity to avoid regressions while a patch is prepared.
- Collected full diagnostic snapshots (attached) for post-incident analysis.

Next steps & timeline:
- 12:30 PDT: runtime patch rollout (targeted) to prevent the fallback regression — COMPLETE.
- 14:00 PDT: controlled reintroduction of previously bypassed nodes and validation under test traffic.
- By EOD today: consolidated incident brief with root cause, corrective actions, and compensatory measures.
- By 2027-06-07: formal postmortem with proposed code, telemetry, and platform changes; we will share for your review.

Customer asks we have noted:
- If Brightleaf needs a credit for SLA impact, we’ll escalate to commercial and follow the agreed service credit process — Ben is on-copy.
- If you require additional data (request ids, request traces) for internal debug, we can provide a redacted bundle.

We take incidents like this seriously. Rishi will continue to own the technical fix; I will own customer communication and the post-incident coordination. Please let me know if you prefer a short call now or a written follow-up — I can schedule a 15-minute sync.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll keep you updated on reintroduction progress.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
